Quick Start

This page describes how to download and install the SDK and run the first example. Prepare an EpicEye camera or virtual camera and ensure that the development computer can reach it over the network.

Download the SDK

Download epiceye_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center, then extract it to a local directory.

epiceye_sdk_<version>/
├── install.sh / uninstall.sh       # Linux
├── install.ps1 / uninstall.ps1     # Windows
├── lib/
├── cpp/
│   ├── linux-x86_64/epiceye_sdk-<version>/
│   ├── linux-arm64/epiceye_sdk-<version>/
│   ├── windows-x64/epiceye_sdk-<version>/
│   └── examples/
├── csharp/
│   ├── EpicEye.SDK.<version>.nupkg
│   └── examples/
├── python/
│   ├── epiceye-<version>-py3-none-any.whl
│   └── examples/
└── docs/                            # Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean

<SDK_DIR> in the following commands refers to the extracted directory.

Requirements

Language Development environment

Python

Python 3.10 or later and pip

C#

.NET 10 SDK

C++

CMake 3.23 or later and a C++17 compiler. Conan is not required to run the bundled examples.

The installation scripts install SDK packages. They do not install Python, .NET, CMake, or a compiler.

Installation Scripts

Linux:

./install.sh --all
./install.sh --python --cpp
./install.sh

Windows PowerShell:

.\install.ps1 -All
.\install.ps1 -Python -Cpp
.\install.ps1
Language Installed content

Python

Installs the bundled Wheel with pip.

C++

Selects the Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64, or Windows x64 package and installs its headers, shared library, and CMake configuration.

C#

Registers the local NuGet source EpicEyeSdkLocal for the bundled EpicEye.SDK package.

C++ is installed to /usr/local on Linux or C:\Program Files\EpicEyeSdk on Windows by default. Use --prefix <directory> or -Prefix <directory> to select another location.

Uninstall:

./uninstall.sh --all
.\uninstall.ps1 -All

Obtain the Camera IP Address

Use the camera search tool or the SDK discovery service. See Camera Discovery and Connection. Examples that connect to a camera accept an optional IP address as the first argument; when omitted, they search for and use the first camera.

Python

cd <SDK_DIR>/python
python examples/capture.py
python examples/capture.py 127.0.0.1:5000

Manual package installation:

python -m pip install <SDK_DIR>/python/epiceye-<version>-py3-none-any.whl

Applications use the SDK through import epiceye.

C++

The bundled CMake project automatically selects the package for the current platform:

cd <SDK_DIR>/cpp/examples
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build --config Release

Linux:

./build/SearchCamera/SearchCamera
./build/EpicEyeCapture/EpicEyeCapture 127.0.0.1:5000

Windows:

.\build\SearchCamera\Release\SearchCamera.exe
.\build\EpicEyeCapture\Release\EpicEyeCapture.exe 127.0.0.1:5000

Application CMake configuration:

find_package(epiceye_sdk CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE epiceye_sdk::epiceye_sdk)

Add -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<install-directory> when using a custom install location.

C#

cd <SDK_DIR>/csharp/examples/EpicEyeCapture
dotnet run
dotnet run -- 127.0.0.1:5000

Add the package to an application:

dotnet add package EpicEye.SDK --version <version>

Without the installation script:

dotnet add package EpicEye.SDK --version <version> --source <SDK_DIR>/csharp

Expected Output

The capture example prints the SDK version, frameID, and processing results. Depending on camera data, it writes image, depth, and PLY point-cloud files.
